Why is sleep so hard? Like, it should be the easiest thing in the world. You're literally just lying there doing nothing. Your body wants to do it, your brain wants to do it, but the second your head hits the pillow your mind decides it's time to replay every embarrassing thing you've ever said. Cool, thanks, brain. Very helpful.

And what's the deal with that thing where you're about to fall asleep and then you jerk awake like you were falling? Your body pranks you! You were so close, right there, and then your own muscles launch you back into consciousness. Rude.

The worst is when you wake up at like 3 AM and you know, you just know, you're not going back to sleep. You're going to lie there for three hours thinking about stuff you can't control, and then finally feel drowsy right when your alarm goes off. Every single time.

But when you get a really good night's sleep? When you wake up actually rested? It's like being a different person. Everything's possible, you're nice to strangers. It's amazing what eight hours can do. Too bad it happens like twice a year.
